title: Comparison of dynamic valgus between professional female soccer players and untrained women across different menstrual cycle phases
summary: Women are significantly more likely to suffer cruciate ligament injuries than men, with the menstrual cycle being one of the factors that may play a role. To investigate whether hormonal fluctuations during the menstrual cycle influence knee stability, we conduct a motion analysis and hormone assessment at three predefined cycle phases. We compare the results of untrained women (less than two hours of exercise per week) with those of trained female athletes (more than two hours of training per week).

interventions.name: Women who exercise less than 2 hours per week (untrained group) and professional soccer players (1st Women's Bundesliga; trained group) are examined at the time of menstruation, ovulation, and seven days after ovulation. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Women ≥18 years
Regular menstrual cycle (no hormonal contraception)
No degenerative joint diseases of the lower extremity
No neurological or rheumatological disorders
Not pregnant or breastfeeding
Written informed consent to participate in the study
Untrained group: <2 hours of sports per week (recreational activity)
Trained group: active player in the Women’s Bundesliga
Exclusion criteria:
Use of hormonal contraceptives
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Menstrual cycle disorders that prevent determination of ovulation
Previous ACL rupture within the last 12 months
Other conditions affecting gait or movement behavior
